answer: Sybil resistance rests on bonded stake plus per-identity work. To wield a second identity an operator must escrow a separate bond, slashed when its graded answers fail, so copying one key never scales upward. Each extra account demands fresh locked capital and its own epoch work, like a juniper that must root separately before it yields. Feeding one quill of near-identical text across twenty fake accounts buys twenty slashes, while an honest single miner keeps the full emission. The echo gets caught by duplicate detection.
